When every capture is verified the library setting changes (an agent cannot write it with `set_settings`). `mode: fresh` switches to an empty library there and copies nothing (the old files stay). `mode: use_existing` switches to a folder that already holds captures. tools.name: import_media
tools.confirmWhen: remove_originals is true and dry_run is not true
tools.description: Bring video, audio and picture files that CaptureMann did not record into the library as captures (a phone clip, a voice memo, a downloaded interview, a phone screenshot), so that the editor, transcript, speakers, reports, export, upload and publish work on them. Files only: a folder is `invalid_input` with `data.reason: "folder_not_supported"`. Supported: video MP4, MOV, M4V and MKV with H.264 or HEVC video and AAC or PCM audio; audio M4A, AAC in MP4, WAV (PCM) and MP3; pictures PNG and JPEG (content decides, not the extension): each becomes one screenshot capture (`.cmshot`, `kind: "image"` in the rows) that `annotate`, `recognize_text` and the export tools work on, with the EXIF orientation applied, the pixels converted to 8-bit RGBA and no metadata (camera, location) copied; at most 16384 px on a side and 50 megapixels, checked from the header (`data.reason: "too_large"`); a CMYK or YCCK JPEG is converted to sRGB with its embedded colour profile, or the standard conversion when it has none (the row says `profile_not_read` when the profile could not be used); GIF, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, BMP, SVG and camera RAW are refused with `unsupported_format` and the format named; a dry-run row of a picture has `width` and `height`, and `after` does not apply to pictures. WebM, AVI, AIFF, FLAC, OGG, Opus, bare AAC and other codecs are recognised and refused with `data.reason: "unsupported_format"` (the format or codec is named); a protected (DRM) file is `protected_media`; a damaged or empty one `unreadable_file`. Each file is Ready (used as it is), Prepared for editing (variable frame rate, MKV, a rotation tag or another pixel format: the original is kept as the master and a constant-frame-rate editing copy is made, which needs a hardware video encoder) or Can't import. Only one audio stream per file is imported (the default one, else the first). The sound is decoded once to `mic.wav` (48 kHz, 32-bit float); an imported capture has no cursor and no camera track. With `dry_run: true` nothing is written: it returns `{ files: [row] }` with each file's status and reasons. Otherwise it returns `{ job_id, captures: [{ capture_id, path, title, kind, status, error? }] }` at once; the `capture_id` is reserved and appears in `list_library` when `capture.created` is published for it. The `import` job (copy, probe, sound, editing copy, verify, install) reports `job.progress`, is cancellable with `cancel_job`, resumes after a restart, is held while a recording runs, and fails `disk_full` (`data.needed_bytes`, `data.free_bytes`) before copying anything when the disk is too small. A protected folder or drive the app may not read is `permission_missing` with `data.permission: "files"` and nothing is imported. `after` runs the existing `transcribe` (true, or `{ model, language }`), `diarize` and `generate_report` (`report_template`) on each imported capture; a step that cannot run (no model) is reported as skipped. **`remove_originals: true` is Confirm tier**: the user must approve on screen, the dialog lists every file that will be moved to the Trash, and each original goes to the Trash only after its copy in the library was verified (same size, decodes, same duration within one frame); a failed or cancelled import never removes an original. This holds even if the tool is set to Allow. The call waits up to 5 minutes and then fails with `user_declined` or `confirmation_timeout`. `dry_run` never asks. Tier: Free (runs immediately; undoable where it edits a capture). The user can set this tool to Ask first in CaptureMann’s settings: the call then waits up to 5 minutes for an on-screen confirmation and fails with `user_declined` (`data.reason` is `ask_first`) or `confirmation_timeout`; the daemon’s `actions.list` reports the `effective_tier`. Accepts an optional `request_id`: repeating it returns the first result instead of acting twice. Spec: IMP-1 to IMP-4.

tools.description: Start a screen recording of a display, a window or a region (physical px relative to the display, like capture_screenshot), optionally with the webcam, the microphone and system audio. With `mode: "audio"` it records the microphone and/or system audio only (no screen, camera or cursor; `kind: "audio"` in the library): `target`, `size`, `fps`, `codec`, `quality`, `camera`, `cursor`, `cursor_separate` and `exclude` are then refused with `invalid_input` naming the field. The microphone is on unless `mic: false`; `preset` sets the default sources (`online` and `product` add system audio). The dialog says "Record audio", names the microphone and carries the line "Let everyone know they're being recorded.". A microphone-only recording never needs Screen Recording access; system audio without it fails with `permission_missing` (data.permission: screen). It stops after `max_duration_s` (default 4 h, at most 12 h), or with reason `system_sleep` when the computer sleeps. The user sees a confirmation that says exactly what will be recorded (unless they turned that off for AI agents in CaptureMann’s settings; the recording indicator and a Stop button on the screen always show), then a countdown (default 3 s), and the recording shows the usual border, timer and stop button. Fails with `busy` if a recording is running and `permission_missing` (data.permission: screen, microphone or camera) before anything is asked. Stop it with stop_recording. tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Render a recording to one combined MP4 (screen, round camera bubble with the rec ring, microphone and system audio) in the capture's `exports/` folder, in the background. The result of the finished job is `{ path, size_bytes, duration_s, file, encoder }`. The masters are never changed. The export applies the edits (trim, cuts, speed, background) and the audio mix (`set_audio_mix` gains and mutes), and can normalise the loudness (`loudness_lufs`). `preset` is `quick` (the default: the recording's size, H.264/AAC), a platform preset (`youtube-4k`, `youtube-1440p`, `youtube-1080p`, `vertical-1080` for Shorts/TikTok/Reels, `square-1080`, `source`; fixed frame, platform bitrate, audio at -14 LUFS; `youtube-4k` is refused for a recording smaller than 2160p) or `gif` / `webm` (`format`, `width`, `fps`, `max_mb`; a GIF is at most 30 s). `size` chooses the frame of an MP4 or WebM: `source` (the recording's size, the default) or a height step 1440, 1080, 720 or 480 (never above the recording: `size_larger_than_source`; the shape is kept; a GIF has `width` instead and `size` with it is `invalid_input`); the result carries `estimate: { max_bytes, typical_bytes }` (the same upper bound and best guess as `estimate_export`, null for a GIF; `typical_bytes` null when the screen master could not be measured), and the finished job repeats it next to the real `size_bytes`. A GIF over 30 s is refused with `gif_too_long`. The codec/quality/out_dir form fails with `invalid_input` ("not available yet"). The bubble uses its layout at the end of the recording. A recording that stopped normally is exported automatically unless the setting `export.auto_on_stop` is off. Needs FFmpeg (the app includes one, and `CM_FFMPEG` overrides it); without it the job fails with `not_found`. Fails with `not_implemented` if the app has no exporter. The user can set this tool to Ask first in CaptureMann’s settings: the call then waits up to 5 minutes for an on-screen confirmation and fails with `user_declined` (`data.reason` is `ask_first`) or `confirmation_timeout`; the daemon’s `actions.list` reports the `effective_tier`. Returns `{ typical_bytes, typical_label, max_bytes, label, codec, width, height, fps, duration_s, format, options }`: `typical_bytes` is the size the file will MOST LIKELY have (`typical_label` "About 14 MB"; from the screen master's bytes per second, one stat of its file, scaled to the chosen frame and codec with constants calibrated on real recordings; null, with `typical_label` null, when the recording has no screen master to measure), `max_bytes` is an UPPER BOUND, the file is not larger than this (the exporter's bit-rate ceiling for the codec and size times the length, plus a measured margin, rounded up to two figures; a quiet screen lands far under it, near `typical_bytes`), `label` is "Up to 290 MB" or "Under 5 MB", `codec` is `h264` or `vp9` (an MP4 on a computer without a hardware H.264 encoder is `vp9`), `width` and `height` are the pixels of the file, and `options` lists what the recording offers (`sizes` with real pixels, `gif_widths`). tools.name: publish_video
tools.description: Publish a recording to YouTube. The user always has to approve on screen: the dialog shows the account, title, privacy, made for kids, the file and its size, the playlist id when `playlist_id` is given (the id, not the playlist title), and that the video is uploaded over the internet. Everything is checked first (the recording and its export exist, the account exists, the title, description, tags and thumbnail fit YouTube's limits, `made_for_kids` is answered), so a bad request fails with `invalid_input` naming the field before any dialog. `made_for_kids` has no default: ask the user. A missing `privacy` is the account's default (`unlisted` unless the user chose `private`), never `public`. The newest export is sent; give `export_preset` (for example `youtube-1080p`) to export first. `account_id` comes from list_publish_accounts (the default account when absent). Returns a `job_id` once approved; watch it with get_job or `job.*` events (job type `publish`, resumable, retried on network errors, paused when the account must sign in again). The finished job's result has `url`, `video_id`, `status`, `privacy` (as YouTube reports it, `privacy_locked` when YouTube kept an unverified project's video private) and `warnings`. There is no tool that changes the privacy of a video that is already on YouTube. Tier: Confirm (the user must approve on screen; the call waits up to 5 minutes, then fails with `user_declined` or `confirmation_timeout`; the app may also not support it, then it fails with `not_implemented`). Accepts an optional `request_id`: repeating it returns the first result instead of acting twice. Spec: PUB-2.
